correctness.rationale: Proof checked across all m≥4, positive real weights and both boundary regimes. Full edge-slope isometry and finite-dimensional numerical-index duality established. The dominant coordinate is a contractively recoverable variable. In the strict polygon regime, the cube-section vertex rule is proved both ways; every restricted coordinate functional is explicitly exposed by q_i=1, q_j=-w_i/(W−w_i). Equal weights give odd/even parity; nonuniform weights are handled by alternating all repeated maxima, using the first smaller weight to enter the strict bound and greedy opposite signs thereafter. The resulting vertex and dual exposed functional violate McGregor exactly when asserted. McGregor is restated and proved in full in arXiv:2604.03690v1. The packaged rational verifier exhaustively tests 1,053 weight vectors and 42,302 vertices within its finite declared range; it is not used as proof for arbitrary weights.

originality.rationale: The full 2023 two-dimensional Lipschitz-free result is confined to three-point metrics; the new theorem explicitly begins with four vertices. The public unit-edge cycle parity result and all-finite-unit-edge-graph bipartiteness result were both read in full and checked to have only unit edge lengths; neither establishes the positive-weight characterization. The full 2018 polyhedral numerical-index paper presents general bounds and special 3D examples rather than the weighted hyperplane dichotomy. The new exact statement detects nonuniform positive perturbations of even cycles and dominated-edge metric degeneracy. Residual unindexed equivalent-language risk is acknowledged; not a uniqueness certificate.
residual_risks: Some unindexed publication in Arens–Eells, transportation-cost, CL-space, or polyhedral-hyperplane terminology might state a logically equivalent all-positive-weight classification; no universal novelty or independent certification claim is made.

value.rationale: Positive-normal central sections of cubes and weighted metric cycles form mathematically canonical continuously parameterized classes, not arbitrary slices. The criterion resolves the entire maximal numerical-index locus over arbitrarily many edges and every real positive weighting. It reveals a sharp metric rigidity invisible to parity alone: an even combinatorial cycle with no redundant edge loses numerical index one under any nonuniform edge perturbation. Exact value below one is not needed for this structurally motivated threshold classification.
